aiRules.rule: Learn by hand. AI (ChatGPT, Claude or any chat assistant) is a tutor only. It can explain, quiz and review, but the trainee types the code.
Build with AI. Any coding agent is allowed (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode).
Explain-back: the trainee must be able to explain every changed line. A mentor checks by pointing at 3 random lines. If they can't explain it, it doesn't merge.
Debug lab with no AI. The one exception is the Week 6 AI patch review, where AI is used only after the bug has been found by hand.
Build days: the afternoon rules apply all day, and explain-back still applies.
No PRs yet: explain-back runs on the day's last commit, and 'How I verified this' goes in the README.

groundRules: In all weekly projects, the goal is to fully test, debug and ship bug-free work.
Weeks 1-5 build one product that grows each week: a booking system for a small business (clinic, gym or salon). Week 6 is a new client problem.
Weeks 1 and 6 start from a client brief and a written scope. Weeks 2-5 start from a short client message, and trainees update the scope before they build.
Postgres runs locally in Docker during development. The production database comes in Week 4, when the app is deployed.
Every project is pushed to GitHub with a README. Every PR has a 'How I verified this' section.
Never paste secrets, API keys or client data into an AI coding assistant. AI features in the product send only the fields they need (no phone numbers or emails) to a provider the client has approved.
Each weekly project has a stretch task for trainees who finish early. Backend concepts carry across languages, so some stretch tasks rebuild a piece in Python, Go or Ruby.
goal: By the end of Week 6, a trainee can take a business problem from a client, scope it, design the architecture, build it full-stack with AI, deploy it on a server, add an AI feature (RAG + tool calling), and demo it. Target roles: forward deployed engineer and full-stack AI developer.
